html:
1What You Will Learn

Note

Acronyms in this note. KMS: Key Management Service; ACM: AWS Certificate Manager; TLS: Transport Layer Security; IAM: Identity and Access Management; ARN: Amazon Resource Name; HMAC: hash-based message authentication code; HSM: hardware security module; FIPS: Federal Information Processing Standards; SSE: server-side encryption; DSSE: dual-layer server-side encryption; EBS: Elastic Block Store; RDS: Relational Database Service; AZ: Availability Zone; ACME: Automatic Certificate Management Environment; ACL: access control list; VPC: Virtual Private Cloud; EFS: Elastic File System; SOC: System and Organization Controls; ISO: International Organization for Standardization; PCI: Payment Card Industry; AMI: Amazon Machine Image; DB: database

  • Encrypt data at rest with AWS KMS and in transit with ACM and TLS
  • Write access policies for data and encryption keys, and rotate keys and renew certificates
  • Implement backups, replication, retention and lifecycle policies
  • Classify data and align services to compliance needs
  • Choose between look-alike services such as KMS and CloudHSM

2Encryption, keys and access policies

Running case

Lantern and Loom Protects the Ledger

  • The shop now holds customer addresses, invoices and an order database
  • An auditor asks: Is it encrypted? Who can read it? Can anyone delete it?
  • A teammate deleted a bucket's contents by mistake
  • Invoices must be kept for seven years
  • Your job: choose the data controls, from keys to backups

The Data Protection Cycle

  • Classify: find sensitive data (Macie)
  • Encrypt: at rest (KMS) and in transit (TLS, ACM)
  • Control access: policies, Block Public Access, key policies
  • Back up and replicate: AWS Backup, snapshots, S3 replication
  • Retain and expire: Object Lock, lifecycle rules
  • Audit: CloudTrail, Config, Artifact

Exam tip

Name the data need first: classify, encrypt, restrict, recover, retain or audit.

AWS KMS Key Types

Key type Who manages it Rotation Cost
AWS owned The AWS service; hidden from you The service decides Free
AWS managed (alias aws/service) AWS KMS for you; you can view it Every year, fixed No monthly fee; per-use fee
Customer managed You: policy, rotation, deletion Optional automatic Monthly fee plus per-use
  • KMS keys are Regional; symmetric keys encrypt data, asymmetric keys hold key pairs
  • Resources under an AWS managed key cannot be shared with other accounts
Exam tip

Control, audit or cross-account sharing means a customer managed key.

Envelope Encryption and Key Policies

  • A data key encrypts the data; the KMS key encrypts the data key; both ciphertexts are stored together
  • A key policy is the main control of a KMS key; the default policy lets the account use IAM policies to grant access
  • Cross-account use needs the key policy and an IAM policy in the other account
  • Grants let AWS services use a key on your behalf
  • Every use is logged in CloudTrail

Exam tip

A KMS key works only if its key policy allows it, directly or through IAM.

Key Rotation and Multi-Region Keys

  • Customer managed symmetric keys: optional automatic rotation, every 365 days by default or a custom period; on-demand rotation too
  • AWS managed keys: automatic every year; you cannot change it
  • Rotation changes the key material, not the key ID or ARN; old material is kept so old data still decrypts
  • Rotation does not re-encrypt your data
  • Asymmetric, HMAC and custom key store keys: rotate manually with a new key and alias
  • Multi-Region keys: related keys in several Regions; rotation is set on the primary key
Exam tip

Rotation is transparent: no code change and no re-encryption.

AWS KMS or AWS CloudHSM?

AWS KMS AWS CloudHSM
What it is A managed key service Your own HSMs in the cloud
Tenancy AWS runs the hardware Single-tenant, general purpose HSMs
Control IAM and key policies You manage keys and users, outside IAM; AWS cannot see key material
Standards Wide service integration FIPS 140-2 or 140-3 level 3 in FIPS mode
Choose it when It is the default You need dedicated HSMs or your own algorithms
Exam tip

Dedicated single-tenant HSMs and full control: CloudHSM. Everything else: KMS.

Encrypting Data at Rest [Verify live]

Service How it is encrypted Watch for
S3 SSE-S3 on every new object by default; SSE-KMS or DSSE-KMS for key control and audit A new default does not re-encrypt old objects
EBS A KMS key; an encryption by default account setting; snapshots stay encrypted Snapshot, then copy encrypted
RDS Chosen at creation; covers storage, logs, backups, replicas Cannot be turned off; encrypt via an encrypted snapshot copy
  • As of 5 November 2026: S3 now disables SSE-C by default on new buckets; check the page
Exam tip

To encrypt an existing unencrypted volume or database, copy a snapshot with encryption on.

Encrypting Data in Transit with ACM [Verify live]

  • TLS encrypts data between clients and services
  • AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) creates, stores and renews public and private certificates; no extra charge for certificates it manages
  • Certificates attach to load balancers, CloudFront and API Gateway; they are Regional, and CloudFront needs its certificate in US East (N. Virginia)
  • An S3 bucket policy can deny non-HTTPS requests and set a minimum TLS version
  • AWS encrypts traffic between Regions and between AZs on its own network
  • As of 5 November 2026: ACM can also issue certificates for other servers through ACME; check the page
Exam tip

A public HTTPS certificate for a load balancer or CloudFront: ACM.

Keeping S3 Data Private

  • Block Public Access has four settings: block public ACLs, ignore public ACLs, block public policies, restrict public buckets
  • Apply at the organization, account, bucket or access point; it overrides policies and ACLs, and the most restrictive setting wins
  • New buckets do not allow public access
  • Object Ownership "bucket owner enforced" (the default) disables ACLs: policies control access
  • IAM Access Analyzer for S3 reviews public and shared buckets
Exam tip

Keep everything private by default: turn on all four settings at the account level.

Access Policies for Data

Goal Control
Only my organization Bucket policy with aws:PrincipalOrgID
Only from my VPC Bucket policy with aws:SourceVpce or aws:SourceVpc, plus a VPC endpoint policy
HTTPS only Deny when aws:SecureTransport is false
Encrypted uploads only Condition on s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption
Use a key from another account Key policy plus an IAM policy
  • A Deny with a condition enforces a rule on every request
Exam tip

An explicit deny with a condition is how you enforce a data rule everywhere.

3Retention, backup, discovery, audit and practice

Retention and Recovery in S3

  • Versioning keeps every version, so an overwrite or delete can be undone
  • Object Lock is write once, read many and needs versioning: compliance mode blocks every user, including root; governance mode lets specially permitted users override
  • A legal hold has no expiry until you remove it
  • Replication: cross-Region (CRR) or same-Region (SRR); live replication copies new objects only; use Batch Replication for existing ones
  • Replication Time Control targets 15 minutes
Exam tip

Cannot be deleted by anyone, even root: Object Lock in compliance mode.

Backups with AWS Backup

  • Backup plans set schedule, retention and lifecycle to cold storage; assign resources by tag
  • Backup vaults hold backups; Vault Lock gives write once, read many protection against deletion
  • Cross-Region and cross-account copies; Organizations policies apply plans to every account
  • Audit Manager reports show compliance
  • Covers EBS, RDS, Aurora, DynamoDB, EFS, FSx, S3 and more

Exam tip

Central, scheduled, cross-Region and tamper-proof backups: AWS Backup with Vault Lock.

Discovering Sensitive Data with Amazon Macie

  • Macie finds sensitive data in S3 with machine learning and pattern matching
  • Managed data identifiers cover personal, financial and credentials data; custom data identifiers use your own patterns
  • It reviews bucket security: public, unencrypted or shared buckets raise policy findings
  • Run automated discovery or discovery jobs, once or on a schedule
  • Findings flow to EventBridge and Security Hub; Organizations manages many accounts
Exam tip

Find personal data in S3 buckets: Macie.

Auditing and Compliance: CloudTrail, Config and Artifact

Service Question it answers Key facts
AWS CloudTrail Who did what, and when? 90 days of event history; trails to S3; CloudTrail Lake for long retention
AWS Config How was it configured, and is it compliant? Configuration history; rules and conformance packs; aggregators for many accounts; remediation
AWS Artifact What does AWS attest? On-demand reports (SOC, ISO, PCI) and agreements; free
Exam tip

Activity: CloudTrail. Configuration: Config. AWS's own reports: Artifact.

Data Lifecycle Policies

  • S3 Lifecycle: transition objects to cheaper classes and expire them; rules apply to existing and new objects and can filter by prefix, tags or size
  • A bucket policy cannot stop a lifecycle rule from running
  • AWS Backup lifecycle: move backups to cold storage, then delete after the retention period
  • Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager: automates EBS snapshots and AMIs: creation, retention and deletion, at no extra cost
  • Keep data as long as rules require, and no longer
Exam tip

Archive then delete on a schedule: lifecycle rules. Scheduled EBS snapshots: Data Lifecycle Manager.

What the Exam Asks: Data Security

  • Which key: AWS owned, AWS managed, customer managed, KMS or CloudHSM
  • Which encryption step: at rest, in transit, rotation or certificate renewal
  • Which access control: Block Public Access, bucket policy condition or key policy
  • Which recovery or retention tool: versioning, Object Lock, replication, Backup or lifecycle
  • Which audit or discovery service: Macie, CloudTrail, Config or Artifact
Exam tip

Look for the verbs: encrypt, restrict, recover, retain, discover or prove.

Design Check: Lantern and Loom Protects the Ledger

Requirement Design
Auditors must see key use and the team controls the policy SSE-KMS with a customer managed key
The order database is unencrypted Encrypted copy of a snapshot, then restore
HTTPS for the site on CloudFront An ACM certificate in US East (N. Virginia)
Only our organization may read a bucket A bucket policy with aws:PrincipalOrgID, and Block Public Access
Invoices kept seven years, never deleted Object Lock in compliance mode
A mistaken delete must be reversible S3 Versioning
Central backups with copies elsewhere AWS Backup with cross-Region copy and Vault Lock
Which buckets hold personal data? Amazon Macie
Show an auditor AWS's ISO report AWS Artifact
  • Cover the right column, answer each row yourself, then compare

4Exam Q&A

4.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer; some ask for two)

S1Lantern and Loom needs full control of a KMS key's policy, rotation and deletion, and wants to share encrypted EBS snapshots with a partner account. Which type of key should it use?

  • AAn AWS owned key
  • BAn AWS managed key such as aws/ebs
  • CA customer managed KMS key
  • DA single-tenant HSM cluster in AWS CloudHSM
Show the answer

Answer: C. Only a customer managed key gives full control of the policy, rotation and deletion, and it can be shared through its key policy. AWS owned keys are hidden, resources under AWS managed keys cannot be shared with other accounts, and CloudHSM is for dedicated HSMs.

S2Order exports in Amazon S3 must be encrypted with a key whose use auditors can follow in AWS CloudTrail, and the team must control the key policy. What should the architect configure?

  • ASSE-S3 default encryption
  • BSSE-KMS with a customer managed key
  • CSSE-C with keys held by the application
  • DNothing, because new objects are encrypted by default
Show the answer

Answer: B. SSE-KMS with a customer managed key logs every key use in CloudTrail and lets the team control the key policy. SSE-S3 and the default give no key-level audit or control, and SSE-C leaves key handling to the application.

S3Which TWO statements about AWS KMS key rotation are correct? (Select TWO.)

  • ARotation changes the key ID, so applications must be updated
  • BAutomatic rotation is optional for customer managed symmetric keys
  • CRotation re-encrypts all the data that the key protects
  • DAfter rotation, data encrypted under older key material can still be decrypted
  • EAWS managed keys rotate only if the customer turns rotation on
Show the answer

Answer: B, D. Automatic rotation is optional on customer managed symmetric keys, and KMS keeps old key material so older data still decrypts. The key ID does not change, existing data is not re-encrypted, and AWS managed keys rotate every year automatically.

S4Lantern and Loom's order database runs on an unencrypted Amazon RDS DB instance. Compliance now requires encryption at rest. What is the correct approach?

  • ATurn on the encryption setting of the running instance and apply it immediately
  • BModify the storage volume of the instance to use a KMS key
  • CAttach a bucket policy to the database that requires encryption
  • DSnapshot the instance, copy the snapshot with encryption, and restore from the copy
Show the answer

Answer: D. An RDS instance can be encrypted only at creation. To add encryption, create a snapshot, copy it with encryption turned on, and restore a new instance from the encrypted copy.

S5Lantern and Loom must keep invoice files for seven years so that no one, including the root user, can delete or overwrite them. Which design meets this?

  • AS3 Object Lock in compliance mode, with versioning and a seven-year retention period
  • BS3 Object Lock in governance mode, with an administrator who may bypass it
  • CA bucket policy that denies s3:DeleteObject to all IAM users
  • DAn S3 Lifecycle expiration rule after seven years
Show the answer

Answer: A. Compliance mode blocks every user, including root, from deleting or overwriting a locked version during retention. Governance mode can be bypassed, a bucket policy can be changed, and a lifecycle rule only deletes.

S6Lantern and Loom wants central, scheduled backups of EBS volumes, RDS databases and DynamoDB tables, with copies in a second Region and protection against anyone deleting the backups. Which solution fits?

  • AManual snapshots that each team creates on its own schedule
  • BS3 Replication on a bucket that holds exported snapshots
  • CAWS Backup with a plan, cross-Region copy and Vault Lock
  • DAWS Config rules that re-create resources someone deleted
Show the answer

Answer: C. AWS Backup centralizes plans across services, copies backups across Regions and accounts, and Vault Lock stops anyone from deleting them. Manual snapshots are not central, and replication and Config do not back up these services.

S7The security team must find out which S3 buckets contain personal data such as names and card numbers, and whether any of those buckets are public. Which service should it use?

  • AAmazon GuardDuty
  • BAmazon Macie
  • CAWS Config
  • DAmazon Inspector
Show the answer

Answer: B. Macie discovers sensitive data in S3 with machine learning and pattern matching, and evaluates bucket security such as public access. GuardDuty detects threats, Config records configuration, and Inspector scans for vulnerabilities.

S8Lantern and Loom serves its site through Amazon CloudFront on its own domain over HTTPS. It wants a certificate that renews automatically at no extra certificate cost. Where should it request the certificate?

  • AIn AWS Certificate Manager, in US East (N. Virginia)
  • BIn AWS Certificate Manager, in the Region closest to customers
  • CIn AWS KMS, as an asymmetric key for the domain name
  • DIn AWS CloudHSM, as a certificate stored in the cluster
Show the answer

Answer: A. ACM issues and renews certificates at no additional charge, and a certificate used with CloudFront must be requested in US East (N. Virginia). KMS and CloudHSM manage keys, not renewing website certificates.

5Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Keys customer managed for control; rotation is transparent; CloudHSM for dedicated HSMs
Encryption SSE-S3 is the default; SSE-KMS for audit; ACM for TLS certificates
Access Block Public Access, bucket policy conditions, and key policies
Retention and recovery Versioning, Object Lock, replication, AWS Backup and lifecycle rules
Prove it Macie, CloudTrail, Config, Artifact
